info.description: Game server panel for Kubernetes that runs Pterodactyl and Pelican eggs.
info.title: Kubedactyl API

get.description: Public: tells the invite page whether the link works and whether the username is fixed.

post.description: Public: creates the account of an invite link (the link works once) and signs it in.
Returns a session token and sets it as HttpOnly cookie. Repeated failures are throttled.

post.summary: Log out (ends the session and clears its cookie)

post.description:
Invalidates every session of the user (including this one). API tokens stay valid; revoke them
separately.

get.description: Public: whether users can sign in through an OpenID Connect identity provider.
get.summary: Single sign-on of the sign-in page

get.description:
Public, opened by the browser: verifies the sign-in, starts a session (cookie) and redirects to
/login?sso=ok&next=<page the sign-in started from>. The account is the one linked to the user of
the identity provider, else the one with the same username, else a new one. Failures redirect to
/login?sso=<reason> (access: in no group with access or disabled, account: the account cannot be
used, failed).

Public, opened by the browser: redirects to the sign-in page of the identity provider, which
returns to /auth/oidc/callback. Failures redirect to /login?sso=failed.
get.summary: Sign in through the identity provider

parameters.description: Page of the panel to open after the sign-in
parameters.name: next

put.description: Invalidates all existing sessions of the user, with revokeTokens also the API tokens.

409.description: the account signs in through single sign-on only

422.description: current password is wrong or the new one is too weak

post.description:
Use it as "Authorization: Bearer <token>". The value is returned only once. Only a session can
create tokens: a token cannot extend its own access.

get.description:
Public (also shown on the sign-in page). The footer always names the software (Kubedactyl).
Sends an ETag: with If-None-Match it answers 304 while nothing changed.
get.summary: Name, tagline, logo and favicon of the panel

get.description:
CRDs, permissions, nodes, metrics-server, load balancer pools and storage classes (cached for 30
seconds).

Kubeconfig or service account in use, authentication method (secrets are never returned), TLS, the
identity reported by the API server (SelfSubjectReview) and the permissions the panel needs.
get.summary: Connection and identity of the panel

get.description:
Nodes with roles, status, capacity, requested resources, live usage (metrics-server) and hardware
(CPU model, vendor, product) plus totals. Ready nodes without hardware data are probed in the
background.

post.description:
Starts a short-lived, unprivileged probe pod on every ready node that reads /proc/cpuinfo and
/sys/class/dmi. Waits for the results (up to 90 seconds).
post.summary: Read the hardware of all nodes again

get.description:
Reads the git repositories set in the settings (eggLibraries). Each is kept in the panel's
memory for 15 minutes; refresh=true downloads them again.
get.summary: List the eggs of the egg library
Get an egg of the egg library

parameters.description: path of the egg file in the repository
parameters.name: path

get.description:
Reads a git repository whether it is configured or not, so the settings can check it
before it is saved. Its eggs are kept in the panel's memory like a listed repository.
get.summary: Check a repository of the egg library

post.description:
Creates an egg from the fields of the editor (also used to duplicate one). The object name is
derived from the display name; a new UUID is assigned.

Accepts a Pterodactyl (PTDL_v1/v2) or Pelican (PLCN_v1-v3) egg as JSON or YAML, either as request
body or as multipart field "file". An egg with the same name is updated.

200.description: an egg with the same name was updated

post.summary: Import an egg from a URL

put.description:
Replaces the fields of an egg. Servers use the changes from their next start (install script: next
reinstall). UUID and import details are kept.

get.description:
yaml / json: Pelican format PLCN_v3 (same content); ptdl: Pterodactyl format PTDL_v2 (JSON).
download=true sends it as file.

post.description:
Downloads the egg from meta.update_url and replaces all fields, including changes made in the
panel. Name and UUID are kept.
post.summary: Update an egg from its update URL

409.description: the egg has no update URL

get.description: Reports whether the panel process is running.
Name, version and run mode (public, so nothing else is revealed).
Open and expired invites, newest first. The links themselves are not stored.

post.description:
The link (/invite?token=<token>) lets someone create an account once within 7 days. The token
is returned only once.

Replaces the link of an invite (the old one stops working) and makes it valid for 7 days again,
also after it expired. The new token is returned only once.

get.description:
Public (also shown on the sign-in page). Markdown; empty when not configured.
Sends an ETag: with If-None-Match it answers 304 while nothing changed.

Averages over the last 5 seconds; refused requests and waiting calls count, too. This request
does not count. Panel is set for administrators only.

post.description: Creates the server and runs the egg install script. Variables are validated against the egg rules.

delete.description: Deletes the server including its data volume.

patch.description: Runtime settings apply on the next start. Disk can only grow.

get.description: Archives in the folder .backups of the server volume, newest first.

post.description:
Packs all server files except the backup folder into a tar.gz in the background. Works while the
server runs.

409.description: a backup or restore is running

post.description:
Deletes all server files except the backup folder and extracts the backup. The server must be
stopped; it cannot be started until the restore has finished.

409.description: server running or job in progress

get.description:
Checks the typical causes why players cannot connect: installation, state, pending restart, disk
space, load balancer address, DNS A/AAAA records of the external domain and the router forwarding
(TCP, tested from inside the network). Users do not see the load balancer IP.

post.description: Starts a background job (see GET /servers/{server}/jobs); its label is the archive's path.
Starts a background job (see GET /servers/{server}/jobs); its label is the archive's path.
post.summary: Extract an archive (zip, tar, tar.gz, tar.xz)

parameters.description: Directory relative to the server root
parameters.name: directory

post.description:
The file container downloads the URL (http/https) into the directory in the background; the
network isolation of the server applies. Existing files are not overwritten.
post.summary: Download a file from a URL

put.description: "to" may contain slashes to move the entry into another folder.

get.description: Does not start the container and does not count as activity.

post.description: Starts the file container of the server if needed and returns its state. Poll GET until ready.

Stops a running job; what it left half done is removed (a cancelled restore leaves the
server files incomplete). A finished job stays as it is.

start, stop (egg stop command or signal, killed after the stop timeout), restart, kill (immediate
SIGKILL).

Stops the server and runs the egg install script again. Files are kept unless the script removes
them.

put.description:
Cron expressions (5 fields or @daily, @hourly, …) use the panel time zone. Tasks run one after
another; the delay waits before a task.
put.summary: Replace the schedules of a server

post.description: Starts the tasks in the background (also for disabled schedules).

get.description:
CPU and memory from metrics-server (cached for 10 seconds), disk usage of the server files (cached
for 30 seconds; the last measured value while neither the file container nor the game runs).

post.description: A suspended server is stopped; its owner can only view it until an administrator unsuspends it.

Moves a stopped server with its data into the namespace of another user. Name, settings, files and
backups stay; the address is fixed to the current one.
post.summary: Transfer a server to another user

409.description: the server is running or already belongs to the user

get.description:
Streams events {"event": "...", "args": [...]}: "console output", "install output", "daemon
message", "status". Send {"event":"send command","args":["say hi"]} or {"event":"set
state","args":["start"]}.
External domain and the storage classes and load balancer pools that can be selected for servers.

put.description:
Every storage class and pool must exist in the cluster; pools must be selectable by service
labels. Missing defaults become the first entry.

get.description:
Cilium LB IPAM pools with their address blocks, usage (also per IP family) and the service labels
that select them.
get.summary: Load balancer IP pools of the cluster

get.description: "required" is true while no active administrator exists; the web UI then shows the setup page.

post.description:
Only possible while no active administrator exists and with the setup token from the panel log.
Signs the new administrator in.

get.description:
Newer chart versions (checked every 10 minutes) and the upgrade jobs. refresh=true checks the
registry now.

post.description:
Starts a job that runs helm upgrade with the release's values and the chosen chart version. The
panel restarts on the new version.

409.description: disabled, unknown version or an upgrade is running

post.description:
Creates the user and its namespace (kubedactyl-user-<username>). The password is stored as
Argon2id hash.

delete.description: Deletes the user, all its game servers, their data and the user namespace.

409.description: last administrator, or managed by the identity provider

message.example: metrics.k8s.io is not available, no CPU and memory usage

method.description: Method: client-certificate, token, exec, auth-provider, basic, service-account or none.

virtualized.description: Virtualized is true when the CPU reports the "hypervisor" flag (VM instead of bare metal).

contexts.description: Contexts lists the names of all contexts in the kubeconfig.

metricsAvailable.description: MetricsAvailable is false when metrics-server does not answer.

path.description: Path of the file in the repository.

repository.description: Repository is the repository URL as configured (https://<host>/<owner>/<repo>).

url.description: URL of the raw file: installing imports it from there and keeps it as update URL.

error.description: Error tells why the repository could not be read (its eggs are then missing).

progress.description: Progress of a running job, once known.

state.description: State is running, done, failed or cancelled.

username.description: Username is ignored when the invite names one.

path.description: Path is the file manager path (download with /files/download?file=…).

storageClass.description: StorageClass and LoadBalancerPool are the defaults of the panel settings.

label.description: Label is appended to the archive name.

externalTrafficPolicy.description: ExternalTrafficPolicy of the service (default Local: the server sees the players' IPs).

ipv6.description: IPv6 also asks for an IPv6 address (dual stack clusters).

loadBalancerIP.description: LoadBalancerIP optionally requests a fixed IP from the pool (one per IP family, separated by a comma).

loadBalancerPool.description: LoadBalancerPool the address comes from (default: the default of the panel settings).

owner.description: Owner is the username the server belongs to (default: the calling admin).

startOnCompletion.description: StartOnCompletion starts the server once the installation is finished.

startupName.description: StartupName picks one of the egg's startup commands ("" = its default).

storageClass.description: StorageClass of the data volume (default: the default of the panel settings).

expiresInDays.description: ExpiresInDays is the lifetime: 1 up to the longest API token lifetime of the panel.

mustChangePassword.description: MustChangePassword makes the user replace the password after signing in.

expired.description: Expired invites stay listed until they are revoked; their link no longer works.

username.description: Username is the name the account gets; empty lets the invited person choose it.

expiresAt.description: ExpiresAt is the end of the token: its own expiry or the longest API token lifetime of the panel.

fields.description: Fields holds validation errors per field or variable.

state.description: State is Stopped, Starting, Ready or Stopping.

stopsInSeconds.description:
StopsInSeconds is how long a ready container stays without further file operations
(reading the session does not count as one).

autoUpdate.description: AutoUpdate turns the hourly update from the URL on (an egg imported again keeps it on).

username.description: Username is set when the administrator chose the name; the invited person cannot change it.

expired.description: Expired invites stay listed until they are revoked; their link no longer works.

username.description: Username is the name the account gets; empty lets the invited person choose it.

error.description: Error tells why the repository could not be read.

url.description: URL is the normalized repository URL.

username.description:
The maximum lengths (usernames have at most 32 characters, auth.MaxPasswordLength) keep a request from
filling the limiters and the log with huge keys.

name.description: Name is shown on the button: "Sign in with <name>".

error.description: Error is set when the pools cannot be read (e.g. Cilium LB IPAM is not installed).

ipv6Missing.description:
IPv6Missing says why servers get no IPv6 address even from a pool with an IPv6 block
("" when they can or it is unknown).
ipv6Missing.example: No IPv6 service CIDR · IPv6 off in Cilium

filename.description: Filename defaults to the last path segment of the URL.

timeZone.description: TimeZone the cron expressions are evaluated in.

cron.description:
Cron is a five-field cron expression ("0 4 * * *") or a descriptor like "@daily",
evaluated in the panel's time zone. Either Cron or Event is set.
+optional

enabled.description: Enabled schedules run automatically; disabled ones can still be run by hand.

event.description:
Event runs the schedule when the server was marked as running ("started") or before it
is stopped or restarted ("stopping"; the stop waits until the tasks are done).
+optional
+kubebuilder:validation:Enum=started;stopping

name.description:
Name identifies the schedule within the server.
+kubebuilder:validation:MinLength=1
+kubebuilder:validation:MaxLength=50

onlyWhenOnline.description:
OnlyWhenOnline skips the run when the server is not running.
+optional

cpuMillis.description: CPUMillis is the current CPU usage (1000 = one core); null when unknown.

diskBytes.description: DiskBytes is the space used on the data volume; null when unknown.

memoryBytes.description: MemoryBytes is the current memory usage; null when unknown.

uptimeSeconds.description: UptimeSeconds since the game pod was started.

allowPrivateNetworks.description:
AllowPrivateNetworks lets game servers reach private networks (other namespaces,
nodes, the Kubernetes API, the LAN). By default every user namespace gets a network
policy that only allows the internet, the cluster DNS and the user's own servers.
+optional

apiTokenMaxDays.description:
APITokenMaxDays is the longest lifetime of an API token (default 90). It also limits the
tokens created before, counted from their creation.
+optional
+kubebuilder:validation:Minimum=1
+kubebuilder:validation:Maximum=3650

brandLogo.description:
BrandLogo and Favicon are images as data URLs (PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP, SVG or ICO, at most
128 KiB); without a logo the built-in one is shown, without a favicon the browser's default.
+optional
+kubebuilder:validation:MaxLength=180000

brandName.description:
BrandName and BrandTagline replace "Kubedactyl" and "Game servers on Kubernetes" in the
sidebar, on the sign-in page and in the browser title (the footer keeps the software name).
+optional
+kubebuilder:validation:MaxLength=40

defaultLoadBalancerPool.description:
DefaultLoadBalancerPool is preselected for new servers (one of LoadBalancerPools).
+optional

defaultStorageClass.description:
DefaultStorageClass is preselected for new servers (one of StorageClasses).
+optional

disableApiDocs.description:
DisableAPIDocs turns the API documentation (Swagger UI at /swagger/) off. The API itself
keeps working.
+optional

eggLibraries.description:
EggLibraries are git repositories (https://<host>/<owner>/<repo>) whose eggs the egg
library on the eggs page lists. The panel reads them when the library is opened and keeps
nothing of them in the cluster.
+optional
+kubebuilder:validation:MaxItems=20

externalDomain.description:
ExternalDomain is shown to users as the server address (domain:port) instead of the
load balancer IP. Empty shows the IP.
+optional

kubeApiQps.description:
KubeAPIQPS is how many requests per second the panel sends to the Kubernetes API at most
(default 50, bursts of twice that). It applies at once.
+optional
+kubebuilder:validation:Minimum=5
+kubebuilder:validation:Maximum=1000

kubeApiUserQps.description:
KubeAPIUserQPS is how many requests per second one user may send to the panel (default 10,
bursts of twice that); each may lead to Kubernetes API calls. More are refused with 429, so
one user cannot use up KubeAPIQPS for everybody. It applies at once.
+optional
+kubebuilder:validation:Minimum=1
+kubebuilder:validation:Maximum=200

legalNotice.description:
LegalNotice (imprint) and PrivacyPolicy are Markdown texts linked in the footer of every
page, also before sign-in.
+optional
+kubebuilder:validation:MaxLength=20000

loadBalancerPools.description:
LoadBalancerPools are the Cilium LB IPAM pools that can be selected for servers.
+optional

oidc.description:
OIDC signs users in through an OpenID Connect identity provider (single sign-on). The client
secret is kept in a Secret, not here.
+optional

oidcClientSecretSet.description: OIDCClientSecretSet tells administrators whether a client secret is stored (always false for users).

serverNotice.description:
ServerNotice is shown to users every time they open one of their servers (plain text).
+optional
+kubebuilder:validation:MaxLength=2000

sessionHours.description:
SessionHours is how long a sign-in lasts (default 12). It applies to every session, so
shortening it also ends older sessions.
+optional
+kubebuilder:validation:Minimum=1
+kubebuilder:validation:Maximum=720

storageClasses.description:
StorageClasses can be selected for server volumes.
+optional

token.description: Token is the one-time setup token from the panel log (or KUBEDACTYL_SETUP_TOKEN).

expiresAt.description: ExpiresAt is the end of the token: its own expiry or the longest API token lifetime of the panel.

revokeTokens.description: RevokeTokens also revokes every API token of the user (after a leak).

externalTrafficPolicy.description: ExternalTrafficPolicy of the service; admins only.

ipv6.description: IPv6 also asks for an IPv6 address (dual stack clusters); admins only.

loadBalancerIP.description: LoadBalancerIP fixes the address: one IP, or one per IP family separated by a comma.

blocks.description: Blocks are the address ranges ("10.0.0.0/24" or "10.0.0.10-10.0.0.20").

isDefault.description: IsDefault is true for the cluster default storage class.

apiVersion.description:
APIVersion defines the version of this resource that this field set
applies to. The format is "group/version" just like the top-level
APIVersion field. It is necessary to track the version of a field
set because it cannot be automatically converted.

fieldsType.description:
FieldsType is the discriminator for the different fields format and version.
There is currently only one possible value: "FieldsV1"

fieldsV1.description:
FieldsV1 holds the first JSON version format as described in the "FieldsV1" type.
+optional

manager.description: Manager is an identifier of the workflow managing these fields.

operation.description:
Operation is the type of operation which lead to this ManagedFieldsEntry being created.
The only valid values for this field are 'Apply' and 'Update'.
+k8s:alpha(since: "1.37")=+k8s:required

subresource.description:
Subresource is the name of the subresource used to update that object, or
empty string if the object was updated through the main resource. The
value of this field is used to distinguish between managers, even if they
share the same name. For example, a status update will be distinct from a
regular update using the same manager name.
Note that the APIVersion field is not related to the Subresource field and
it always corresponds to the version of the main resource.

time.description:
Time is the timestamp of when the ManagedFields entry was added. The
timestamp will also be updated if a field is added, the manager
changes any of the owned fields value or removes a field. The
timestamp does not update when a field is removed from the entry
because another manager took it over.
+optional

annotations.description:
Annotations is an unstructured key value map stored with a resource that may be
set by external tools to store and retrieve arbitrary metadata. They are not
queryable and should be preserved when modifying objects.
More info: https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/overview/working-with-objects/annotations
+optional

creationTimestamp.description:
CreationTimestamp is a timestamp representing the server time when this object was
created. It is not guaranteed to be set in happens-before order across separate operations.
Clients may not set this value. It is represented in RFC3339 form and is in UTC.

Populated by the system.
Read-only.
Null for lists.
More info: https://git.k8s.io/community/contributors/devel/sig-architecture/api-conventions.md#metadata
+optional
+k8s:alpha(since: "1.37")=+k8s:immutable

deletionGracePeriodSeconds.description:
Number of seconds allowed for this object to gracefully terminate before
it will be removed from the system. Only set when deletionTimestamp is also set.
May only be shortened.
Read-only.
+optional
+k8s:alpha(since: "1.37")=+k8s:optional
+k8s:alpha(since: "1.37")=+k8s:immutable

deletionTimestamp.description:
DeletionTimestamp is RFC 3339 date and time at which this resource will be deleted. This
field is set by the server when a graceful deletion is requested by the user, and is not
directly settable by a client. The resource is expected to be deleted (no longer visible
from resource lists, and not reachable by name) after the time in this field, once the
finalizers list is empty. As long as the finalizers list contains items, deletion is blocked.
Once the deletionTimestamp is set, this value may not be unset or be set further into the
future, although it may be shortened or the resource may be deleted prior to this time.
For example, a user may request that a pod is deleted in 30 seconds. The Kubelet will react
by sending a graceful termination signal to the containers in the pod. After that 30 seconds,
the Kubelet will send a hard termination signal (SIGKILL) to the container and after cleanup,
remove the pod from the API. In the presence of network partitions, this object may still
exist after this timestamp, until an administrator or automated process can determine the
resource is fully terminated.
If not set, graceful deletion of the object has not been requested.

Populated by the system when a graceful deletion is requested.
Read-only.
More info: https://git.k8s.io/community/contributors/devel/sig-architecture/api-conventions.md#metadata
+optional
+k8s:alpha(since: "1.37")=+k8s:optional
+k8s:alpha(since: "1.37")=+k8s:immutable

finalizers.description:
Must be empty before the object is deleted from the registry. Each entry
is an identifier for the responsible component that will remove the entry
from the list. If the deletionTimestamp of the object is non-nil, entries
in this list can only be removed.
Finalizers may be processed and removed in any order.  Order is NOT enforced
because it introduces significant risk of stuck finalizers.
finalizers is a shared field, any actor with permission can reorder it.
If the finalizer list is processed in order, then this can lead to a situation
in which the component responsible for the first finalizer in the list is
waiting for a signal (field value, external system, or other) produced by a
component responsible for a finalizer later in the list, resulting in a deadlock.
Without enforced ordering finalizers are free to order amongst themselves and
are not vulnerable to ordering changes in the list.
+optional
+patchStrategy=merge
+listType=set

generateName.description:
GenerateName is an optional prefix, used by the server, to generate a unique
name ONLY IF the Name field has not been provided.
If this field is used, the name returned to the client will be different
than the name passed. This value will also be combined with a unique suffix.
The provided value has the same validation rules as the Name field,
and may be truncated by the length of the suffix required to make the value
unique on the server.

If this field is specified and the generated name exists, the server will return a 409.

Applied only if Name is not specified.
